name: Mei Zhan
description: A highly versatile Fujian cultivar, originally from Anxi. While it can be made into a pleasant oolong, it has gained modern fame as one of the primary cultivars used to produce Jin Jun Mei, an elite, bud-only black tea from the Wuyi region. Its inherent sweetness and fruity notes make it an excellent base for high-end black teas.
plantType: Vigorous, semi-arbor type with good adaptability (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Highly adaptable to different terroirs within Fujian, which has contributed to its widespread use.
processing: Mei Zhan's versatility is due to its balanced chemical composition. Its buds are particularly well-suited for black tea processing, as they are rich in compounds that create sweetness and a thick texture when fully oxidized.
oxidation: Oxidation is typically full (100%) for its most famous black tea expression. When made as an oolong, it undergoes medium oxidation (30-40%).
roasting: Roasting is not a key feature. Black tea expressions are simply dried. Oolong expressions may receive a light bake.
versatility: Extremely versatile. It is a rare cultivar that can be skillfully crafted into high-quality oolong, black, and even white tea, though its modern fame is overwhelmingly tied to black tea.

china: Other provinces like Zhejiang and Sichuan

Black Tea.Jin Jun Mei: Its most prestigious modern use. The tender buds are crafted into a high-end black tea with notes of honey, fruit, and sweet potato.

Oolong Tea.Mei Zhan Oolong: Can be made into a fragrant Anxi-style or Wuyi-style oolong, though this is less common now.

White Tea.Mei Zhan Buds: Its downy buds can be processed into a sweet, fruity white tea.

sensory.aroma: Honey, sweet potato, fruity (as black tea); Floral, fruity (as oolong)
sensory.flavor: Very sweet, mellow, and complex with a smooth finish and no astringency.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, full, and often thick and syrupy, especially as Jin Jun Mei. The liquor is a beautiful golden-orange.
